summary: Round six. The four round-five items are answered in the scanner: java.io and java.util.zip are real PACKAGES now, ALLOWED carries the byte/checksum types that makes that possible, .now(Zone...) and .exec( are entries, and the ALLOWED docstring says prefix. MEASURED at the staged bytes in a throwaway worktree: new java.io.PrintStream("/x"), java.util.zip.ZipFile, javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory, java.net.MulticastSocket and java.net.InetAddress.getByName are all refused; java.net.URI/URLEncoder, Clock.class, a Clock parameter, LocalDate.now(clock), dataFiles.size() and Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() are all accepted; the real tree passes with 101 scanned files, and the backlog's 103 tracked / 2 exempt / 11 implements counts all reproduce exactly. The package half now holds against every sibling I could name inside the six packages. Three majors remain. (1) The entry added THIS round to close R5-2 matches the sample's spelling rather than the overload it names: LocalDate.now(zone), where zone is a field of type ZoneId, reaches the real clock and passes -- and the entry's own comment claims to cover the JDK's now overloads that do not take a Clock. (2) ALLOWED is outside ALL_ENTRIES and unpinned by any case, so the carve-out that makes the package ban true can be widened silently: MEASURED, adding 'java.io.File' to it lets new java.io.File(p).delete() pass in ingest while the PrintStream case still refuses and the count still prints 21. The backlog cell says an entry cannot be added without evidence; for this list it can. (3) check-io-seam.sh's own header still describes the design round five falsified -- five families not six, no java.util.zip, 'the java.io File types', java.io.InputStream 'untouched', and '.now( closes the factory family in one entry', which is both false (two entries) and exactly the gap in finding 1. No production code and no object-store request is touched: the gate reads source text and adds zero requests of any kind. Two minors and a nit.

findings.title: the zone-overload entry matches the SAMPLE's spelling, not the overload: LocalDate.now(zone) reaches the real clock and passes
ALLOWED is not in ALL_ENTRIES and is pinned by no case, so the carve-out that makes the package ban true can be widened in silence
the gate's own header still describes the round-four design: five families, no java.util.zip, 'the java.io File types', and '.now( closes the factory family in one entry'
findings.failure_scenario:
Read against scripts/io_seam_scan.py at the same staged bytes. The header says: '`java.nio.file`, `java.nio.channels`, `java.net`, `javax.net` and the `java.io` File types are forbidden outright'. PACKAGES holds SIX entries and `java.util.zip` is one of them -- a reader of this header concludes `new java.util.zip.ZipFile("/x.zip")` is unlisted, when it is refused (measured, exit 1). And 'the `java.io` File types' is the class-name-prefix framing round five MEASURED as false -- the whole point of this round is that java.io is a PACKAGE ban with a named carve-out, and the header states the design that let PrintStream through. Two sentences later: '`java.io.InputStream` is likewise untouched: moving bytes is not I/O' -- InputStream is not untouched, it is banned-and-then-excepted by ALLOWED, which is the distinction that makes the package bannable at all and the one a reader most needs from this file. And '`.now(` closes the factory family in one entry where naming five of the nine `java.time` types did not' is false twice over: the list carries TWO now entries ('.now()' and '.now(Zone...)'), and the family is not closed -- R6-1 walks through the same sentence.

Concrete failure: this header is what an author reads at the moment the gate refuses them, and it is the file the backlog row points at as one of the two headers carrying the honest scope. It under-states what is banned (so a reviewer checking 'is zip covered?' answers no from the wrong file) and it re-asserts, in the enforcing script, the exact claim shape that five rounds of review were spent removing from four other documents. AGENTS.md, code-structure.md, the backlog row and io_seam_scan.py all say six packages; only the gate that runs them says five.

findings.title: 'MEASURED as exactly the eight java.io types and CRC32 this tree uses' describes a list holding ten java.io entries, three zip entries and three java.net entries
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED on the staged tree: `git ls-files '*/src/main/java/binjava/*.java' | grep -v '^binstore-backends/' | xargs grep -o 'java\.io\.[A-Za-z]*'` yields exactly eight distinct types -- IOException, UncheckedIOException, InputStream, OutputStream, ByteArrayInputStream, ByteArrayOutputStream, FilterInputStream, Closeable -- plus CRC32 from java.util.zip, and ZERO java.net types. The measurement is true; the list beside it is not what was measured. ALLOWED holds TEN java.io entries (adding FileNotFoundException and Flushable), THREE java.util.zip entries (adding Adler32 and Checksum) and three java.net entries, so four names are in the carve-out that the sentence 'MEASURED: exactly the eight `java.io` types below and `CRC32` appear in non-exempt `src/main`, and nothing else' says are there because they were measured. None of the four opens a reach -- they are an exception, a marker interface and two checksums -- which is why this is minor and not R6-2. Concrete failure: the next reader checking whether the carve-out is still minimal counts ten names under a sentence promising eight, and cannot tell which entries carry measurement and which carry a guess -- in the one list whose narrowness is the argument that the package ban is safe. Say it as it is: the eight measured, plus four named forward for types that reach nothing.

findings.title: the stated blind spots are reflection, a dependency and the exempt module; JDK filesystem and socket APIs outside the six packages are none of those and pass
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED at the staged bytes, three files written under ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/, all compiled clean by javac 25, all staged, gate exit 0 in the same run:

    new java.util.logging.FileHandler(path, true)     // creates and writes a real file
    java.sql.DriverManager.getConnection(url)         // opens a real socket
    ClassLoader.getSystemResourceAsStream(name)       // the sibling of the banned .getResourceAsStream(

None is reflection, none is a third-party dependency, none is inside binstore-backends -- so none is covered by the three blind spots both documents enumerate, and the third is a direct sibling of a DISK entry the list already carries. The two halves are described as 'the package half' (closed by construction) and 'the clock and the subprocess' (hand-named), which leaves a reader with no category for a filesystem or socket reach through java.util.logging, java.sql, java.util.prefs or javax.imageio. The construct list in fact already carries four DISK/SOCKET entries (.getResourceAsStream(, .toURL(, .openStream(, .openConnection() for exactly this reason, so the two-halves framing does not match the list it describes. I am NOT asking for those packages to be banned -- that is the treadmill the row is right to refuse. The honest sentence is that the package half is closed against SIBLINGS INSIDE the six packages, not against JDK I/O generally, and the blind-spot list gains a fourth item. Concrete failure: an author reads 'the package half is closed by construction', concludes that a green gate means business logic reaches no file, and stops looking -- which is the precise reliance round five's PrintStream finding showed is placed on these sentences.

findings.title: the 'THE OPENING CALLS ARE STILL BANNED' paragraph is duplicated verbatim inside the ALLOWED comment
findings.failure_scenario: The five-line block beginning '⚠️ THE OPENING CALLS ARE STILL BANNED, so allowing `URI` opens no route' appears twice in the same comment, once before and once after the prefix-matching paragraph, identical to the character. Harmless today; the cost is that the next edit to that argument changes one copy, and this file's comments are the artifact the row treats as load-bearing -- a claim stated twice and maintained once is how the 'closed by construction' sentence survived in four documents after the code stopped supporting it.

findings.title: logic() puts java.nio.file.Path in the fixture signature, so every sample in everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED is refused before its body is read
findings.failure_scenario: `logic(body)` emits `Object go(java.nio.file.Path p, java.time.ZoneId z, char c)`, which itself matches the java.nio.file package ban. So the `assertThat(r.exit()).isEqualTo(1)` half of the loop holds for all 21 samples regardless of the body -- the only assertion carrying weight is `r.out()).contains(e.getKey())`. That is still a real constraint for 20 of the 21 (deleting a shape stops its name being printed), which is why this is minor, but for the `java.nio.file` sample itself both assertions are satisfied by the fixture's own parameter list: the body `java.nio.file.Files.exists(p)` could be deleted entirely and the case would stay green. Concrete failure: the loop reads as 21 independent refusals and is 20 plus one that tests the harness; a future edit that narrows the java.nio.file entry to something that no longer matches a bare type reference is invisible here. Cheap fix: take Path out of the signature (`Object go(java.time.ZoneId z, char c)`) so the refusal a sample buys is the sample's.
